_note: FICTIONAL TEST DATA for the Echo Legacy engine (CS 413). Every person, place, business and entry here is invented. Team: Peter Paul Poloan — Front End, Back End, Q/A, UI/UX Designer, Documentator (one-member group).

entries.text: Maria turned sixteen today. Carmen's sister baked her an ube cake and the whole house smelled of it.
Opened Dela Cruz Hardware at seven. Sales were slow but two contractors asked for quotes.
Visited Carmen's grave with the kids after mass. Adam Jr. lit the candles and did not say a word.
The store stayed closed for the lockdown. Paid the two helpers anyway from our savings.
Maria called from Manila. She got into the nursing program and cried on the phone. So did I.
A new supplier from Lipa offered better prices on cement. Signed a six-month contract.
Check-up with the doctor. Blood pressure is high again. I must cut down on salt and coffee.
Took Maria and Adam Jr. to the beach in Caramoan. Maria swam out farther than I liked.
First Valentine's without buying flowers for Carmen. Left a rose by her photo instead.
Profit this quarter is the best since we opened. Thinking about a second branch near the market.
Noche Buena at home. Maria brought a friend from the hospital. We sang until past midnight.
Argued with the supplier about late deliveries. Customers are drifting to the big store at the mall.
Maria passed the nursing board exam. I told everyone who came in today, some of them twice.
Adam Jr. wants to run the store someday. He is good with customers but careless with the ledger.
Three days in the hospital. Lito handled the store and the bank. I trust him with the keys.
Maria and I walked along the beach in Daet. She asked about her mother and I told her the old stories.
Decided not to open the second branch. Sales are fine, and my health matters more now.
Adam Jr. and his wife are expecting. My first apo! Carmen would have cried with joy.
Maria visited with flowers. I told her I am writing letters she will read someday.

entries.title: To my daughter
entries.text: Anak, if you are reading this, it is already May 2040. I am proud of the nurse you became and of the kind person you always were. Keep your mother's ube recipe and make it for your own children. Love, Papa.
